title: Embedding vector dimension & reindex playbook for schema upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: As we onboard higher‑capacity embedding models and re-evaluate quality-vs-cost tradeoffs, we need a safe, repeatable migration path for changes to embedding vector dimensionality and the associated index schema. This ticket defines an engineering playbook: detection, schema versioning, client-facing compatibility, reindexing strategies, rollout phases, rollback, and observability. Goal: enable dimension changes (both increases and decreases) with minimal customer breakage and predictable latency/cost impact.

Background & motivation: Customers and model teams require flexibility to upgrade to newer embedding models (e.g., 1024→1536 dims or 1536→2048 dims) which often improve retrieval/re-ranking quality but increase storage, indexing, and distance compute cost. A naive full reindex is expensive and may cause prolonged downtime or degraded throughput for large customer indexes. We need documented alternatives (full reindex, lazy reindex-on-read, shadow index + dual-read) and evaluation criteria so PMs and Solutions Eng can choose the right approach per customer.

Scope: This playbook covers server-side index schema changes in our embeddings storage layer and reranking pipeline, API response changes required for client compatibility, migration tooling, and operational runbooks for scaling and diagnosing regressions. It does NOT cover model training or canonical model selection; it assumes a new model dim is already chosen upstream.
acceptance_criteria: API returns schema_version and vector_dim in embedding metadata for all new responses
Migration modes documented and tested: full-reindex, lazy-reindex-on-read, shadow-index-dual-read
Automated reindex job can process 1M vectors/day in test cluster with monitoring and throttling
SDKs handle padded/truncated vectors with clear deprecation path and tests for backward compatibility
Canary rollout procedure executed on internal test org without regression in rerank recall metrics
steps: Design: finalize schema_versioning approach (immutable version field + index metadata) and vector_dim header semantics
Prototype: implement server-side projection API that can optionally map old-dim vectors to new-dim via linear projection matrix (experimental, for quick compatibility)
Tooling: build reindex worker with pause/resume, concurrency controls, and throughput shaping; add dry-run mode that simulates storage and CPU cost

Migration modes: implement three strategies - (A) full-reindex (recommended for small/medium datasets), (B) lazy reindex-on-read (migrate entry when first accessed), (C) shadow index + dual-read (writes to both; read fallback)
API changes: embed schema_version and vector_dim in embedding response JSON and in response headers; document SDK behavior for mismatched dims
Rollout: test internal canary -> beta customers opt-in -> gradual ramp; monitor L2 rerank metrics and tail latency
Rollback: ability to route traffic back to old index and revert schema_version flag if quality regressions or latency regressions exceed thresholds
comments: 2026-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial playbook after model team requested 1536→2048 migration. Added three migration strategies and initial acceptance criteria.
2026-02-20 - Marcus Lee: Implemented prototype of schema_version header and vector_dim in dev API. Observed 18% storage increase for 1536→2048 on sample dataset (200k vectors).
2026-02-24 - Maria Gomez (PM): Raised client impact concerns for customers with on-device embeddings pipelines. We should add explicit SDK deprecation notices and a mapping guide.

2026-02-27 - Engineering review: Decided to build server-side linear projection as a stopgap only. Projection will be opt-in and labelled experimental in docs. Quality risk: projection reduces recall by ~5-8% in initial tests.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Lee: Reindex worker v0.2 supports pause/resume and per-customer rate caps. Integration tests added; CI job simulates 1M vector reindex in 18 hours on staging cluster (configurable).
2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Preparing canary on internal analytics org next week. Need product approval for customer opt-in messaging and billing adjustments (storage change).
notes: Trade-offs: Full reindex is highest quality but highest cost. Lazy reindex reduces immediate cost but skews early traffic to older vectors until warmed. Shadow-index dual-read provides immediate consistency but doubles write cost until old index is retired.

Projection approach: fit a linear mapping W between old_dim and new_dim using a held-out seed set. Pro: avoids immediate reindexing; Con: measurable quality drop and potential licensing/privacy considerations if projection depends on a sample corpus.

Client SDK impact: SDKs must accept variable-length vectors and expose vector_dim in response objects. For now we will support zero/right-padding on client side for consumers that cannot accept variable length; deprecate padding within 6 months.
Observability: add metrics - reindex_progress_pct, reindex_bytes_processed, projection_calls, avg_vector_dim_per_request, index_storage_bytes_by_version, rerank_recall_by_index_version

Performance targets: aim for <5% 99th percentile latency increase in our reranking endpoint during steady-state migration; storage overhead target <2.2x when moving from 1024->2048 using quantization defaults.
Docs & customer comms: Solutions Eng to prepare migration playbook, estimated cost calculator, and example opt-in request template for large customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Latency regression at tail when reindex jobs saturate IO. Mitigation: rate-limit reindex workers and use background IO class; add circuit breaker for rerank service.

Risk: Client SDKs break if they assume fixed vector dims. Mitigation: add clear runtime schema_version and vector_dim, SDK updates with graceful fallback, and a 3-month deprecation window for older SDKs.

Risk: Quality regressions after projection. Mitigation: require A/B on recall and precision for projected vectors vs reindexed baseline; projection is opt-in and only used where acceptable delta < 6% recall drop.
Risk: Increased cost for customers. Mitigation: publish cost estimator, offer limited-time credits for migration, and allow customers to schedule off-peak reindex windows.
